claims.verbatim:
Steamship Hansa (Brem), Van Oterendorp, Bremen Sept
9, via Southampton 12th, with mdse and 816 passengers, also
$119,250[?] in specie, to Oelrichs & Co. Sept 13, off the Lizard,
saw an American steamer; 14th, lat 49 40, lon 12 06, saw ship
Dunmore (Br); lat 49 44, lon 13 10, ship Garnett; 15th, lat 49
40, lon 17 50, a British steamer, brig rigged, bound E, and at
the same time ship Mary Ann Holman; 16th, lat 49 32, lon 21[cut]
44, steamship Allemania; 24th, lat 41 48, lon 63 03, spoke bark
Honduras (of Kingston, Ja), from Liverpool for New York;
on the 22d, in a hurricane, she had lost her mainmast, fore-
topgallantmast and mizzentopmast, all her boats and sails,
and was much strained, but her captain hoped to reach New
York; left her after providing her with a boat and some
stores; weather at the time fine and wind fresh from the
eastward.

claims.claim: Spoken / sighted Sandy Hook 220 miles E of Sandy Hook (9th 7:30 AM)
claims.citation: New York Herald, 11 September 1866, p. 8, col. 6
claims.verbatim:
Steamship Hermann (Brem), Wenke, Bremen Aug 26, via
Southampton 29th, at 5 PM, with mdse and 767 passengers,
to Oelrichs & Co. Had strong westerly gales on the pass-
age. Aug 29, off the Needles, passed steamship New York,
hence for Bremen; 2d inst, lat 51, lon 29, ship Transit, bound
W; 6th, lat 45, lon 52, a National Company's steamer, bound
E; 7th, lat 43, lon 60 30, steamship Persia, hence for Liver-
pool; same day, steamship Palmyra, bound E; 9th, 7:30 AM,
220 miles E of Sandy Hook, steamships Allemania, America,
and City of New York, bound E.
